newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Gambia opposition chief says four supporters held.
newsitem.headline: Gambia opposition chief says four supporters held.

text.p: Gambia's opposition chief Oussainou Darboe said on Monday police arrested four of his followers after breaking up a welcoming party at his home.
Darboe said police beat up his supporters who welcomed him at Banjul airport on his return from Botswana on Saturday and then travelled in a motorcade for a party at his residence.
The four were held at Kombo police station outside Banjul.
No police comment was immediately available and it was not clear if the procession had been authorised.
Darboe, a prominent lawyer, was the most serious civilian candidate in presidential elections last September won by then military ruler Yahya Jammeh.
As votes were counted he took refuge at the Senegal embassy, emerging days later to say he feared for his safety.
Darboe's United Democratic Party is the largest opposition group in parliament with seven deputies. Jammeh's party counts 33 of the assembly's 45 elected members.
Both Jammeh and Darboe were in Botswana last week for a Commonwealth regional meeting on democracy.
